notes:
Account: large historical news/media archive (video transcripts + scanned PDFs) spanning ~18M articles + 2M long-form transcripts. Primary ask: end-user search that's fast and precise for research analysts. They currently use a hybrid SQL+Elastic stack; want improved relevance using embeddings + supervised reranker. Quoted: 'Search must surface the exact clipping/quote within long transcripts — snippet precision matters more than novelty.'

Key constraints: average document length 20k-40k tokens; many OCR artifacts; preservation of original timestamps and source metadata required for compliance. Extremely cost-sensitive at high QPS (expected 4k qps during peak ingest/search periods). Latency SLO goals: median 120ms for vector lookup + top-N candidate fetch, end-to-end 250-350ms when including lightweight reranker for common queries. For deep contextual reranking (full cross-encoder) they accept 600-800ms in non-interactive batch flows.

They asked about Redwood features: automatic chunking strategies, prefix KV caching, model variants for CPU/GPU, and canary rollouts for reranker model updates. Strong appetite for Dedicated or Private deployment (VPC + customer KMS) because of licensing and archive PII concerns.

indexing_estimate: ~20M documents after chunking (avg chunk size 1.5k tokens); expected vector index size ~6TB compressed
chunking_strategy_notes: Testing 1k, 1.5k, 2k token windows with metadata-stable boundaries (speaker change, paragraph breaks). Preference for semantic chunker + overlap 128 tokens for reranker context. Plan: two-tier index: short-chunk dense vectors for recall + document-level coarse index for provenance and filtering.
reranker_tuning_notes: Proposal: bi-encoder retrieval for top-200 candidates, then a lightweight cross-encoder reranker tuned on in-domain Q/A pairs. Evaluate margin/loss weight for relevance vs. hallucination. Concern: full cross-encoder on 200 candidates is expensive — experimenting with distilled reranker or cascaded reranking (fast classifier then cross-encoder top-25).
latency_target: vector lookup <=120ms; lightweight rerank end-to-end <=350ms for interactive; batch deep rerank windows <=800ms
cost_per_query_target: $0.002 - $0.01 (depends on reranker depth); POC target $0.005 avg
vector_db_preferences: Open to Milvus or managed index (Redwood suggestions). Want benchmarked e2e performance numbers with their dataset prior to commitment.
notes_quote: 'If we can't get 75% of answers in the top 10 we won't replace Elastic' — research lead (M. Gomez).
poC_feedback: Good relevance lift; biggest ops pain: ingest normalization and reranker hyperparameter drift. Want automated eval hooks (eval sets + regression alerts) before production rollout.

short_summary: Novella Vault Solutions evaluating Redwood Dedicated/Private for large-scale RAG search over long-form media archives. Focus: embeddings + cascaded reranking to hit interactive latency and cost targets while preserving provenance and residency controls. Current POC shows promise; blockers are legal/residency and final latency/cost benchmarking.
